question: Should authenticated Webhooks routes now fail closed for every `childSessionKey` that is neither the exact bound session key nor a recorded child/parented session, including legacy callers that supplied unrelated keys?
rationale: This is an externally observable compatibility change, but it restores the documented route-session authority boundary and prevents cross-session task ownership from being accepted.

options.title: Adopt the fail-closed route-tree contract
options.body: Rebase the PR, reject the `current` sentinel, and document HTTP 403 as the intentional behavior for unrelated legacy child-session keys.

options.title: Preserve legacy behavior behind explicit policy
options.body: Keep the existing permissive behavior by default only if maintainers accept the cross-session capability and introduce a clearly named, documented strict mode.

recommendation.title: Adopt the fail-closed route-tree contract
recommendation.body: Rebase the PR, reject the `current` sentinel, and document HTTP 403 as the intentional behavior for unrelated legacy child-session keys.

likelyOwner.reason: The affected boundary crosses the Webhooks plugin and shared session-visibility SDK, but reliable feature-history attribution was unavailable in this read-only review environment.
